payload.prompt: Which actions belong to the Foundry app development workflow?

options.rationale: Choosing a model from the Model Catalog is part of the workflow. It happens after signing in and creating a Foundry project.

options.text: Deploy the selected model.
options.rationale: Deployment makes the selected model available for use. It comes before testing and using the configured model in a client application.

options.text: Test prompts and responses in the Playground.
options.rationale: The Playground is used to write prompts and test model responses. Developers can also configure parameters there.

options.text: Run inference on every user request as the server.
options.error_type: confuses development workflow with server responsibilities
options.rationale: Running inference is what the server does after receiving a prompt. It is not a setup action in the Foundry development workflow.
options.better_fit: This fits server responsibilities.

feedback.intrinsic: The learner would mix setup steps with what happens later when the app is already sending requests.
feedback.instructional: The workflow prepares the model for use; the server runs inference during client-server interaction.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The workflow moves from project setup to model choice, deployment, Playground testing, and app use.

payload.prompt: Which tasks are client responsibilities in an AI client application?

options.text: Present a UI or CLI.
options.rationale: The client presents the user interface or command-line interface. That is how the user interacts with the application.

options.text: Format user input into a prompt or API request.
options.rationale: The client collects user input. It then formats that input into a prompt or API request before sending it.

options.text: Display the returned output.
options.rationale: After the server returns output, the client displays it. This completes the user-facing part of the interaction.

options.text: Apply system instructions and safety to the model response.

options.rationale: The server applies system instructions, safety, context, and more. The client is responsible for sending the request and displaying the returned output.

feedback.instructional: Keep client and server duties separate: the client handles the user flow, and the server handles inference and safety context.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The client handles input, request formatting, sending, and display.
